outcome.technical: WHAT CHANGED. (1) _runner_output.py: every tally now carries `passed`. house: N of `N/M`. pytest: its `passed` word alone, plus `skipped` and `xfailed`. unittest: `Ran N` minus failures, errors, skipped, expected failures and unexpected successes, read off both the FAILED (...) and the new OK (...) line (`_UNITTEST_OK`), plus `skipped` and `xfailed`. jest and vitest summaries, playwright line and JSON, vitest JSON: the runner's own passed figure. sweep_tally: its cases. The mixed tally: 0. No existing key changed value, so red reads the same collected/failed/assertions it read before. (2) stamp-verification.py green. Newness is read by house_case_id: a passing label whose id HEAD's own run printed for no case. A label with no id counts only through the PASSED count rising (_own_by_id). Whole labels are never compared. The count reading (_case_counts) takes tally['passed']. A rise made only of skips is could-not-prove, and _skipped_clause says skips never ran. An expected-failure count above HEAD's own run is not-green. _not_green_failure: a non-zero exit with one runner's tally showing collected > 0 and failed > 0 is not-green, whatever the assertion count. The basis names the failing cases and no longer says 'reached no verdict'. That wording is kept only for no tally, a mixed tally and zero collected. Zero collected now also requires no skips. _baseline_labels: a HEAD run that printed no tally, beside a house task run, is an empty list of labels, so --case applies to a new house file. support_held_clause is green's own support sentence; red keeps support_clause. _green_baseline_clause says what made the baseline green: stubs, absent JS files, a new stage. The section comment above GREEN_WORDS is rewritten to the new rule. (3) One set-up, one baseline step and one teardown, called by both verbs: _proof_setup (scope, sized deadline, budget, overlays, leftovers, env, digests, holder plus owner file, interrupts armed), _proof_preflight (fit, HEAD's files, inline problem), _baseline_files (new/absent/stubs/stages), _baseline_run (build, the 'building the throwaway spent the deadline' sentence, start_problem, the baseline run with head['absent'] set), _proof_teardown and _left_behind (the junction clause). run_green now passes `stages` to green_verdict and reports `baseline` in its payload as red does. outcome.descriptive: Green-first now proves only cases of the task's own that ran and passed on the base: by case id or a passed count, never by whole label, skips or expected failures. A test that raises on the base is not-green. A new JS file or stage block proves through the baseline step red and green now share with their set-up and teardown.
